feedback: Compensation I made: the five sensors now span ±0.036 m, so I rescaled sensor weights to x/0.018 (giving [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]) instead of x/0.012. This cuts the signal per metre of offset by about one third. I raised kp from 3.0 to 3.5 and kd from 0.3 to 0.4 to hold steering gain near baseline on the narrower 0.10 m track. Evidence from iteration 0: max_error sat at about 0.06 m on every track (the off-track limit), and line_loss_events were 1.0 to 1.35 per run, so the tape was lost at the sensor edge. Evidence that spread is the main limit: the oval finish rate was only 0.05, and 19 of 20 oval runs ended off track. If the next race shows line_loss_events still at 1.0 or more and max_error still near 0.06, the sensing span is still too narrow. Widen the spread further to ±0.05 m (five sensors at x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05), or raise sensor_size to 0.016 m to see the tape at larger offsets. If the next race shows steering_oscillation rising well above the baseline 0.13 to 0.29 range while line losses fall, the sensors are too far ahead and react late. Move the sensor y values from 0.04 toward 0.02 m. If line losses fall but max_error stays near 0.06 with no oscillation, the limit is controller lag rather than sensing, so try moving the sensors forward to y = 0.06 m instead of widening further.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events remain at 1.0 or more and max_error stays near 0.06 m, widen the sensor lateral spread to ±0.05 m (x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05). The baseline loses the tape at about 0.042 m offset, and the wider span is the only lever that addresses that edge.

If line losses remain high after the spread change, raise sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m. A larger footprint keeps the tape visible further off centre, which is the cause of the blind spots in iteration 0.

If steering_oscillation rises well above the baseline (0.13 to 0.29) while line losses fall, move all sensor y values from 0.04 to 0.02 m so the sensors react closer to the axle. If line losses fall and max_error stays near 0.06 with no oscillation, move sensor y forward to 0.06 m to reduce controller lag.
